editorial.headline: The Fine Line in Selling Floors and Furnishings
editorial.standfirst: A retail activity open nationally to full foreign ownership, yet unavailable for PMA registration anywhere in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the retail trade in the finishing elements that give an interior its texture and atmosphere: carpets and rugs, curtains and drapes, and wall and floor coverings such as wallpaper, tiles, laminate and vinyl flooring. Its boundary matters. The activity expressly does not extend to retailing the building-material category of floor tiles, laminate and vinyl. In practice, the registration should reflect the retail offer as it is actually presented, with the distinction between interior coverings and the excluded building-material retail activity kept clear.

The activity is open to businesses at every stated scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth makes it relevant to a modest specialist shop as well as to a larger-format retail operation. The common thread is not the size of the premises or catalogue, but the retail sale of the named furnishing and covering products. A business built around carpets, window dressings, wallpaper, and eligible floor-covering lines belongs in this commercial frame when those goods are the substance of its retail activity.

Nationally, the position is straightforward. The activity is classified as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. A foreign investor can therefore hold the full permitted ownership interest at the national level. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national openness, however, is not the whole operating picture for an investor considering Bali.

In Bali, a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA today. The Bali status is Blocked (risk class): at the Besar scale, every scope is assessed in OSS at Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk, bringing the activity within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. The block has applied under the Bali moratorium since May 2026. For this activity, national permission to reach 100% foreign ownership does not translate into a PMA registration route in Bali.
